constraints_addressed: Pilots must be read-only and use historical records
controls: Any future pilot must use historical records and cannot update HR systems.

pilot.agent_role: Classify request type and flag missing information without deciding eligibility or policy outcomes.
exit_criteria: Stop if classification accuracy is below 75 percent, reviewer agreement is below 80 percent, or any employee-data control breach occurs. Go if at least 60 historical cases achieve at least 93 percent classification accuracy and at least 95 percent reviewer agreement. Revise if classification accuracy is 75 to 92 percent or reviewer agreement is 80 to 94 percent.
pilot.first_step: HR Onboarding Manager decides whether the two request types share one boundary.
pilot.human_role: HR reviewers decide routing, completeness, eligibility, and all follow-up actions.
pilot.narrow_scope: Historical read-only shadow of 60 employee-service records with no HR system changes.
pilot.objective: Measure request classification and missing-field detection after HR confirms the process boundary.

validation_questions: Should onboarding and benefits requests share one process boundary or remain separate?
Who owns benefits intake and which system receives routed requests?
Which employee-data controls apply to a historical sample?

value_case.basis: The two mapped records list 3,850 annual requests, but they represent different request types and have no shared rework, error-cost, or savings baseline.
value_case.label: medium

opportunities.why_now: A deployed onboarding check and an idea-stage benefits intake show recurring employee-service demand, but ownership, systems, and a common process boundary are incomplete.
